rendered: The review starts from the total known global cobalt reserves, taken from the United States Geological Survey report on cobalt: ≈7 million[1]. It then applies a conservative yearly mining efficiency of ≈70%[2], and assumes that only a share of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing, ≈40%[3]. Applying these factors, the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the reserves falls to ≈2 million[4], so the review concludes that Co demand would exceed the cobalt available for battery manufacturing before 2045[5] unless Co-free cathodes or recycling are adopted. The review's own recomputation states: ≈2 million metric tons globally[6].
